title: Yaadon Ki Baaraat
source_material: Original
character_social_background: Younger version of Ratan (played as an adult by Tariq Khan)
role_gist: Credited as Master Aamir, the eight-year-old plays the younger Ratan in the flashback built around the title song 'Yaadon Ki Baaraat Nikli Hai', which shows the brothers as children before they are separated. The appearance is brief and has no independent arc; the adult Ratan is played by Tariq Khan.
character_arc: Not applicable (brief child role)
recognition: Described as the first quintessential masala film; popularised the separated-siblings-reunited formula and launched the careers of Zeenat Aman, Neetu Singh and Tariq Khan.
research_notes: Release date 9 November 1973 per Wikipedia; Bollywood Hungama lists 3 November 1973. Wikipedia gives box office of ₹5.5 crore (Box Office India) without a nett/gross label, so it is not entered; annual rank 5 refers to that unlabeled measure.

title: Madhosh
character_social_background: Younger version of Raj Kumar (played as an adult by Mahendra Sandhu)
role_gist: Aamir Khan is credited as the younger version of Raj, the lead played by Mahendra Sandhu, in a 1974 drama produced by Tahir Hussain. The sources consulted carry no plot summary and do not describe the child role, so the character's function in the film is unverified beyond the cast credit.
character_arc: Not applicable (brief child role)
research_notes: Exact release date, writers, box office and reception not found. Wikipedia's article is a stub flagged as needing a plot summary.

title: Holi
source_material: Based on a play by Marathi playwright Mahesh Elkunchwar
character_social_background: Student in a college hostel
role_gist: Madan is one of the restless hostel students whose boredom and resentment of the principal escalate into a campus revolt. He joins the protest, is suspended, is implicated after a classmate's suicide and is arrested. The largely improvised parallel-cinema ensemble gave Aamir Khan his first adult screen role, credited as Aamir Hussain.
principal_motivation: Rebellion against the college authorities
principal_conflict: Student protest against the principal and its fallout
character_arc: Bored participant in hostel pranks becomes implicated in tragedy
character_outcome: Suspended and arrested
critical_reception: Vincent Canby (The New York Times, 1985) found it decently and exuberantly performed by its largely non-professional cast.
recognition: Wikipedia lists a National Film Award for Best Cinematography (Jehangir Choudhary), flagged as needing a citation.
research_notes: No budget or box-office data found. Production company not stated.

title: Raakh
producers: Asif Noor; Sangeeth Sivan; Aditya Bhattacharya
source_material: Original screenplay
character_occupation: Aimless young man who becomes a vigilante
character_social_background: From a well-off family, leading an otherwise mundane life
role_gist: Amir is a fearless but aimless young man whose older, more pragmatic girlfriend Neeta is raped by the crime boss Hassan Karmali while he is forced to watch. Guided by a disillusioned policeman, he sets out to wipe out the Karmali family, growing used to violence and even enjoying it. Neeta slowly rebuilds her life; Amir ends on death row.
principal_motivation: Revenge for the assault on Neeta
principal_conflict: Rage at an unjust system against guilt over his own violence
character_arc: Innocent, fearless youth becomes a hardened killer
character_outcome: Awaits execution on death row
critical_reception: Strong critical acclaim; developed a considerable cult following.
recognition: Three National Film Awards, including a Special Mention for Aamir Khan (shared with Qayamat Se Qayamat Tak); Bollywood debuts of cinematographer Santosh Sivan and editor A. Sreekar Prasad.
research_notes: Shot before but released after Qayamat Se Qayamat Tak. Wikipedia gives box office of ₹15 million (₹1.5 crore) citing Talking Moviez, without a nett/gross label; not entered.

title: Love Love Love
character_social_background: Poor household with his father, stepmother and sister
role_gist: Amit, a student from a poor family, falls for his wealthy schoolmate Reema, who is coveted by the violent Vicky. Vicky and his father threaten Amit's family and force the lovers apart, and Amit is humiliated at Reema's engagement party. The couple flee, Amit survives an assassination attempt, and they are reunited after Reema's father kills both antagonists.
principal_motivation: Love for Reema across the class divide
principal_conflict: A violent rival and threats against his family
character_arc: Humiliated poor lover persists and survives to win Reema
character_outcome: Reunited with Reema
critical_reception: Did not match the expectations set by the pair's debut film but was appreciated by viewers.
recognition: Second film of the Aamir Khan–Juhi Chawla pairing.
research_notes: Wikipedia gives box office of ₹2.8 crore citing Indicine, without a nett/gross label; not entered. Budget not found.

title: Awwal Number
character_occupation: Cricketer newly selected for the national team
character_social_background: Up-and-coming player replacing an established star
role_gist: Sunny is a young cricketer picked for India in place of the established star Ronny, who turns vengeful. As DIG Vikram Singh races to stop a terrorist plot to bomb an India–Australia match, Sunny weathers Ronny's hostility and becomes a star by playing the match-winning stroke. A light romance with Aarti offers him emotional support.
principal_motivation: Prove himself in international cricket
principal_conflict: Rivalry with the displaced star Ronny amid a terror plot
character_arc: Untested newcomer becomes a match-winner
character_outcome: Wins the match for India
critical_reception: A 2019 retrospective blog review treats the film as unintentionally comic.
research_notes: Second-billed after Dev Anand. The romance with Aarti (Ekta Sohini) is documented only through the 'I love you' recorder scene, so no Romances row was created. Bollywood Hungama's 1 January 1990 date is a placeholder; Wikipedia's 11 May 1990 is used. No box-office data found.

title: Tum Mere Ho
writers: Tahir Hussain, M. Kaleem Rahi (screenplay); Tahir Hussain, Surinder Singh (story)
character_social_background: Foundling raised by a poor snake charmer after surviving a serpent's revenge as a baby
role_gist: Shiva survives a shape-shifting serpent's revenge as a baby and is raised by a poor snake charmer. His music enchants Paro at a fair and they fall in love, but her family reveals she was married as a child and must live as a widow, and her father sends men to kill him. Shiva finally uses his charmer's powers to force the serpent to undo her curse.
principal_motivation: Love for Paro
principal_conflict: Paro's family, the child-widow custom and the serpent's curse
character_arc: Cursed foundling becomes a charmer powerful enough to defeat the serpent
character_outcome: Defeats the serpent; union with Paro implied but not confirmed by sources
critical_reception: A box-office disaster later enjoyed as a so-bad-it's-good cult film; one 2019 review credits it with using snake tropes to dramatise patriarchal custom.
research_notes: Wikipedia and The Cultural Gutter describe Shiva's origin differently (his father kills the snake versus a stranger stealing its crown); the shared elements are used. The ending is not stated explicitly in either source. No budget or box-office figures found.

title: Dil
writers: Naushir Khatau (story, screenplay); Rajeev Kaul, Praful Parekh (screenplay); Kamlesh Pandey (dialogue)
character_social_background: Son of Hazari Prasad, a miserly and greedy wastepaper businessman
role_gist: Raja, the spendthrift son of a miserly scrap dealer, meets the arrogant heiress Madhu at college, fakes blindness to fool her and trades pranks with her. After she falsely accuses him of attempted rape and he rebukes her, they fall in love. Disowned by both fathers, they marry secretly and live in poverty; when Raja is injured, his father tricks Madhu into leaving, but they reunite.
principal_motivation: Love for Madhu
principal_conflict: Both fathers' greed and class pride
character_arc: Pleasure-seeking prankster becomes a hard-working husband
character_outcome: Reunited with Madhu
critical_reception: Positive reviews, with praise for the soundtrack and cast performances.
recognition: Madhuri Dixit's first Filmfare Best Actress award; soundtrack sold about 2 million units; remade in Telugu (Tholi Muddu) and Kannada (Shivaranjani).
research_notes: Wikipedia gives two release dates (15 and 22 June 1990); the infobox date 22 June is used, matching Bollywood Hungama. Box office 'est. ₹20 crore' (Box Office India via Wikipedia) has no nett/gross label and is not entered.

title: Deewana Mujh Sa Nahin
source_material: Remake of the 1986 Pakistani film Beyqaraar
role_gist: Ajay, a photographer at a modelling agency, becomes convinced that his colleague Anita returns his love, though she sees him only as a friend. When she becomes engaged to Vikram, Ajay keeps preparing to marry her anyway, and she must act to stop his obsession. Events expose that Vikram does not love her and that Ajay's devotion is sincere, and the film ends happily with them together.
principal_motivation: Marry Anita
principal_conflict: Anita does not love him and is engaged to Vikram
character_arc: Deluded, fixated admirer is finally accepted
character_outcome: Wins Anita
research_notes: No budget, box-office, reception or award data found. Plot detail comes from a short Wikipedia synopsis.

title: Jawani Zindabad
source_material: Remake of the Kannada film Avale Nanna Hendthi (1988)
character_social_background: Family scarred by dowry: his elder sister died a dowry victim
role_gist: Shashi, whose elder sister died as a victim of dowry, vows never to give or take dowry. Defying his mother, he marries Sugandha without any dowry, then takes on the greedy in-laws of his younger sister Rama, led by the politician Goverdhan Verma. Seriously injured in the confrontation, he survives to see Goverdhan reform.
principal_motivation: End the dowry practice that killed his sister
principal_conflict: Protecting Rama from her in-laws' greed
character_arc: A principled young man holds to his vow against family pressure and political power
character_outcome: Survives serious injuries; Goverdhan reforms
research_notes: Marriage to Sugandha is documented, but not how they meet. No box-office, reception or award data found.

title: Afsana Pyar Ka
producers: Manoj Seksaria; Sanjay Seksaria; Arvind Seksaria
character_social_background: Raised by his father Mahendra Behl, apart from the mother who left him as an infant
role_gist: Raj and Nikita meet at college and, after early misunderstandings, fall in love without knowing their families share a long-standing feud. Raj also does not realise that the college's new principal is the mother who left him with his father. When both families forbid the marriage and arrange other matches, the couple decide to elope.
principal_motivation: Marry Nikita
principal_conflict: Feuding families refuse the match
character_arc: A college romance becomes open defiance of both families
character_outcome: Elopes with Nikita; later events not verified
research_notes: The family backstory and elopement come from web search summaries of IMDb-style plot synopses. The songs 'Nazren Mili' and 'Tip Tip Tip Tip Baarish Shuru Ho Gayi' were popular. No box-office data found.

title: Daulat Ki Jung
source_material: Inspired by Mackenna's Gold (1969)
character_social_background: Son of the wealthy businessman Bhushan Chaudhry
role_gist: Rajesh, the son of a wealthy businessman, loves his classmate Asha, whose father is his father's business rival. When both fathers clamp down on them, the couple elope in a stolen car and stumble into a treasure hunt around a tribal village, pursued by crooks. An undercover police officer disposes of the criminals and the lovers are united.
principal_motivation: Be with Asha
principal_conflict: Rival fathers and treasure-hunting criminals
character_arc: Sheltered rich son becomes a fugitive lover
character_outcome: United with Asha
research_notes: Release date 17 January 1992 per Wikipedia; Bollywood Hungama lists 3 January 1992. Runtime, writers and box-office figures not found.

title: Jo Jeeta Wohi Sikandar
source_material: Original; resemblance to Breaking Away (1979) noted after release
character_social_background: Middle-class son of Ramlal Sharma; younger brother of the college's star cyclist Ratan
role_gist: Sanju is a carefree Model College student living in the shadow of his brother Ratan and the elite Rajput College. He fakes wealth to date the rich Devika, ignoring his loyal friend Anjali's warnings, and is humiliated when exposed. After Ratan is badly injured in the rivalry, a chastened Sanju takes his place in the inter-college cycle race and wins it in the final seconds.
principal_motivation: Status and fun, later redemption for his brother and father
principal_conflict: Class rivalry with Rajput College and its champion Shekhar
character_arc: Irresponsible show-off becomes a disciplined, humbled champion
character_outcome: Wins the cycle race for Model College
critical_reception: The Indian Express (1992) praised the cinematography, sets and performances of Aamir Khan, Ayesha Jhulka and Pooja Bedi but criticised the music.
recognition: Cult following; often cited among the best Indian coming-of-age films. Filmfare Best Film.
research_notes: Wikipedia gives India box office of ₹70 million (₹7 crore), citing Bollywood Hungama and Box Office India, without a nett/gross label; not entered.

title: Isi Ka Naam Zindagi
source_material: Remake of the Bengali film Banchharamer Bagaan (1980), based on Manoj Mitra's play Shajano Bagaan
character_social_background: Grandson of Bansiram, who guards a coveted plot of land
role_gist: Chhotu is the grandson of Bansiram, an old man who refuses to surrender a prized plot of land to successive heirs of a zamindar family. The film's weight rests on Pran's Bansiram, and later comment describes Aamir Khan's part as largely inconsequential, relegated to songs and a romance with Chumki. No detailed account of Chhotu's own arc was found.
critical_reception: Pran's performance was singled out and used to promote the film.
research_notes: Billed first but functions as a co-lead to Pran. Wikipedia gives box office of ₹18 million (Indicine) without a nett/gross label; not entered. No Romances row because the relationship with Chumki is undocumented beyond the cast list.

title: Damini
producers: Karim Morani; Bunty Soorma; Aly Morani
writers: Rajkumar Santoshi (story, screenplay); Sutanu Gupta (story); Dilip Shukla (dialogue)
role_gist: Aamir Khan appears as himself in the stage-show dance number 'Bin Sajan Jhoola Jhoolu' in Rajkumar Santoshi's legal drama. The appearance doubles as promotion for his then-upcoming Santoshi film Andaz Apna Apna and has no narrative function. The drama itself, led by Meenakshi Seshadri and Sunny Deol, is regarded as a cult feminist film and won National Film and Filmfare awards.
critical_reception: Universal acclaim for its execution and performances; regarded as a cult feminist film.
recognition: National Film Award for Best Supporting Actor (Sunny Deol); Filmfare Best Director, Supporting Actor, Story and Sound.
research_notes: Wikipedia's 'est. ₹11.75 crore' box office has no nett/gross label and is not entered.

title: Parampara
writers: Honey Irani (story, screenplay); Aditya Chopra (screenplay); Rahi Masoom Raza (dialogue)
character_social_background: Son of Prithvi Singh and the gypsy woman Tara, raised in the Thakur household after her death
role_gist: Ranvir, son of Prithvi Singh and the gypsy woman Tara, grows up in the Thakur household alongside his half-brother Pratap. On learning who ordered his mother's execution, he turns on Pratap and a violent feud engulfs the family. After the patriarch's death the brothers embrace and the bloodshed ends.
principal_motivation: Justice for his mother's death
principal_conflict: Feud with his half-brother Pratap over the family's past
character_arc: Unaware youth becomes vengeful, then reconciles
character_outcome: Reconciles with Pratap
critical_reception: Largely negative reviews; one review singled out Aamir Khan's performance while calling the younger cast out of place.
research_notes: Neelam (Sapna) and Raveena Tandon (Vijaya) appear, but no source consulted documents a romantic pairing for Ranvir, so Principal Female Lead is left blank and no Romances row was created. Saif Ali Khan's Hindi film debut. No box-office figures found.

title: Hum Hain Rahi Pyar Ke
writers: Robin Bhatt (story, screenplay, dialogue); Aamir Khan (screenplay, dialogue)
source_material: Based on Houseboat (1958)
character_occupation: Runs a garment company under pressure to deliver a large shirt order
character_social_background: Guardian of his late sister's three mischievous children
role_gist: Rahul, struggling to run a garment business and control his late sister's three unruly children, agrees to marry the businessman Bijlani's daughter Maya for the children's sake. The children secretly shelter Vyjayanti, who has escaped her father's confinement, and she wins them over and then Rahul. Surviving sabotage by the spurned Bijlanis and her tradition-bound father's resistance, Rahul marries Vyjayanti.
principal_motivation: Keep the business afloat and give the children a stable home
principal_conflict: Obligation to the Bijlanis against love for Vyjayanti
character_arc: Stern, overwhelmed guardian becomes a warm father figure and partner
character_outcome: Completes the order despite sabotage and marries Vyjayanti
critical_reception: Positive reviews, with particular praise for Juhi Chawla's performance.
recognition: National Film Awards: Special Jury Award (Mahesh Bhatt) and Best Female Playback Singer (Alka Yagnik). Filmfare Best Film and Best Actress. Soundtrack sold 2.5 million units. Remade in Telugu and Malayalam.
research_notes: Aamir Khan co-wrote the screenplay and dialogue. Wikipedia's ₹97 million box office (Box Office India) has no nett/gross label and is not entered.

title: Pehla Nasha
writers: Neeraj Vora (story); Ashutosh Gowariker (screenplay); Sanjay Chhel (dialogue)
source_material: Remake of Body Double (1984)
role_gist: Aamir Khan appears as himself in a scene with Shah Rukh Khan, Saif Ali Khan, Rahul Roy and Sudesh Berry in Ashutosh Gowariker's directorial debut, a remake of Body Double. It is noted as the only film to put Aamir, Shah Rukh and Saif Khan in a single scene; the cameo has no narrative role.
critical_reception: Negative reviews.
research_notes: First collaboration with Ashutosh Gowariker as director. No box-office figures found.

title: Andaz Apna Apna
alternate_identity: Uses the alias Teelu; feigns amnesia and blindness
character_social_background: Lives with his father Murli Manohar
role_gist: Amar, a lazy daydreamer, sets out to marry the heiress Raveena Bajaj for her father's money and meets his match in the equally scheming Prem. Unaware that Raveena and her secretary Karishma have swapped identities, he falls for the woman he believes is the heiress. Through feigned amnesia, rival cons and a villainous twin, he ends up marrying the real Karishma for love.
principal_motivation: Get rich by marrying an heiress
principal_conflict: Rivalry with Prem for the heiress
character_arc: Gold-digger falls genuinely in love and becomes a reluctant hero
character_outcome: Marries Karishma
critical_reception: Unsuccessful on release; later praised as one of the greatest Hindi comedies (Raja Sen, Khalid Mohamed).
recognition: Cult classic; voted second-best Bollywood comedy in an Indian Express online poll; 4K re-release on 25 April 2025.
research_notes: Box Office India via Wikipedia: budget ₹29 million, domestic ₹8.18 crore, overseas US$150,000, worldwide gross ₹8.653 crore. The domestic figure is recorded as gross because it plus overseas approximates the worldwide gross. Release date 4 November 1994 per Wikipedia; Bollywood Hungama lists 3 September 1994. Raveena Tandon plays Karishma, the secretary posing as the heiress; she is Amar's partner.

title: Baazi
writers: Ashutosh Gowariker; Neeraj Vora; Naushil Mehta (writers); Santosh Saroj (dialogue)
source_material: Original; critics likened it to Die Hard
alternate_identity: Goes undercover in drag as Miss Julie Braganza
character_social_background: Son of a police inspector; both parents were murdered by Chaubey
role_gist: Inspector Amar, whose parents were murdered by the politician Chaubey, investigates a multi-crore scandal and is framed for killing the police commissioner's daughter. Hunted, he works undercover, including in drag as Miss Julie Braganza, and fights through a hostage siege that endangers journalist Sanjana. He electrocutes Chaubey in the climax and is honoured by the Chief Minister.
principal_motivation: Expose the scandal and avenge his parents
principal_conflict: Framed and hunted by a powerful politician
character_arc: Dedicated officer becomes a fugitive and avenger
character_outcome: Kills Chaubey and is honoured
critical_reception: Mixed reviews; India Today called it an ambitious collage of Die Hard, Point Break and Rambo that 'just doesn't work'.
research_notes: Budget ₹32.50 million; box office 'est. ₹88 million' (boxofficeindia.com via Wikipedia) has no nett/gross label and is not entered. Release date 14 April 1995 per Wikipedia; Bollywood Hungama lists 13 April.

title: Aatank Hi Aatank
source_material: Heavily inspired by The Godfather (1972)
lyricist: Naqsh Lyallpuri; Anwar Sagar; Sanam Ghazipuri; others
character_occupation: Son of a crime boss who becomes one himself
character_social_background: Younger son of the crime patriarch Shiv Charan Sharma
role_gist: Rohan, the younger son of crime patriarch Shiv Charan Sharma, has kept away from the family business until his father is shot. He takes revenge on the rival Gogia Advani, goes on the run, and four years later has become a crime lord alongside his brother Munna. His girlfriend Neha and a later attraction to Ganga sit at the margins of this Godfather-inspired gang war.
principal_motivation: Avenge the attack on his father
principal_conflict: Gang war with rival dons
character_arc: Outsider son becomes a crime lord
research_notes: Second-billed after Rajinikanth. Relationships with Neha (Juhi Chawla) and Ganga (Pooja Bedi) are documented only as one-line cast descriptions, so no Romances rows were created. Ending, box-office figures and reviews not found.

title: Rangeela
writers: Ram Gopal Varma (story, screenplay); Neeraj Vora, Sanjay Chhel (dialogue)
character_social_background: Streetwise Mumbai orphan (tapori)
role_gist: Munna, a streetwise orphan who sells cinema tickets on the black market, has loved his childhood friend Mili for years without saying so. When Mili starts working with the star Raj Kamal, Munna's sense of inferiority deepens as she spends her days with Raj, and every attempt to confess fails. He writes a farewell letter and leaves town, but Mili reads it and, with Raj's help, reaches him.
principal_motivation: Love for Mili
principal_conflict: Cannot confess his love while a film star seems to offer Mili a better life
character_arc: Insecure tapori finds the courage to reveal his feelings
character_outcome: Reunited with Mili
critical_reception: Critical acclaim, with particular praise for A. R. Rahman's soundtrack and Urmila Matondkar's performance.
recognition: Landmark film credited with a modern sensibility in mid-1990s Hindi cinema; Filmfare wins for Supporting Actor, Music Director, Story, Costume and Choreography; BFJA Best Actor (Hindi) for Aamir Khan.
research_notes: Wikipedia's ₹33.4 crore box office (Box Office India) has no nett/gross label and is not entered. Release date 8 September 1995 per Wikipedia; Bollywood Hungama lists 9 August 1995.

title: Akele Hum Akele Tum
source_material: Loosely based on Kramer vs. Kramer (1979)
role_gist: Rohit, an aspiring playback singer, marries Kiran despite her parents' opposition, and her own ambitions recede into housework while his career stalls. Too proud to accept her support, he reads it as pity; she leaves to build a career while he raises their son Sunil alone. She wins custody in court but chooses not to separate father and son, and the family reconciles.
principal_motivation: Success as a singer and a stable family
principal_conflict: Wounded pride as his wife's career overtakes his
character_arc: Proud, struggling artist becomes a devoted single father
character_outcome: Reconciles with Kiran
critical_reception: Both leads' performances were acclaimed.
recognition: Eight Filmfare nominations; soundtrack sold about 2.5 million units, the year's ninth-highest seller.
research_notes: Wikipedia's ₹12.37 crore box office (Box Office India) has no nett/gross label and is not entered. Release date 1 December 1995 per Wikipedia; Bollywood Hungama lists 30 November.

title: Raja Hindustani
producers: Ali Morani; Karim Morani; Bunty Soorma
writers: Dharmesh Darshan (story); Robin Bhatt (screenplay); Javed Siddiqui (dialogue)
source_material: Inspired by Jab Jab Phool Khile (1965)
character_social_background: Working-class driver in the small hill town of Palankhet
role_gist: Raja, a proud small-town taxi driver, is hired by the wealthy Aarti, who has come to Palankhet to find traces of her late mother. They fall in love and marry over her father's objections, but her scheming stepmother Shalini convinces each that the other wants out. Separated, Raja takes their infant son, fearing Aarti will keep him away; the deception is exposed and the family reunites.
principal_motivation: Love for Aarti and his self-respect
principal_conflict: The class gap and the stepmother's conspiracy
character_arc: Proud working-class lover survives separation and misunderstanding to reunite his family
character_outcome: Reunited with Aarti and their son
critical_reception: Mixed: Anupama Chopra (India Today) found it dated but called Karisma Kapoor its lifeblood; the lead pair's chemistry was praised.
recognition: Five Filmfare Awards including Best Actor for Aamir Khan; seven Screen Awards; soundtrack sold 11 million copies; fourth-highest domestic grosser of the 1990s.
research_notes: All commercial figures from Box Office India via Wikipedia. Overseas gross is not stated separately and is not derived.

title: Ishq
writers: Praful Parikh, Rajiv Kaul (story, screenplay); Tanveer Khan (dialogue)
character_social_background: Working-class; best friend of the wealthy Ajay
role_gist: Raja, a working-class mechanic, is best friends with the rich Ajay. Raja falls for Madhu, the heiress whom the fathers want Ajay to marry, while Ajay loves the poor Kajal. Both fathers, contemptuous of the poor, use bribes and fake photographs to turn the couples against each other. Raja exposes the scheme, and Ajay and Madhu reach the departing ship just in time to reunite with their true partners.
principal_motivation: Love for Madhu and loyalty to Ajay
principal_conflict: Two rich fathers' schemes against cross-class marriages
character_arc: Comic underdog outwits the fathers
character_outcome: United with Madhu
critical_reception: Mixed to positive; praised for humour, soundtrack and performances, criticised for story and screenplay.
recognition: Soundtrack sold about 3 million units; remade in Kannada as Snehana Preethina (2007).
research_notes: Raja is paired with Madhu (Juhi Chawla) and Ajay (Ajay Devgn) with Kajal (Kajol), per the verbatim plot and cast lines. Commercial figures from Box Office India via Wikipedia.

title: Ghulam
source_material: Based on On the Waterfront (1954)
lyricist: Indeevar; Nitin Raikwar; Sameer; Vinod Mahendra
character_social_background: Mumbai neighbourhood youth; younger brother of Jai, right-hand man to the gangster Ronnie
role_gist: Siddhu, an aimless amateur boxer, drifts on the edges of the gang run by Ronnie, whom his brother Jai serves. He wins a reckless dare against an oncoming train, falls for Alisha, and unwittingly lures her brother Hari, a social worker, into a fatal ambush. Losing Alisha and then Jai, he confronts his family's history of cowardice, testifies against Ronnie and beats him in a public boxing bout.
principal_motivation: Redemption and standing up to Ronnie
principal_conflict: Loyalty to his brother against his conscience
character_arc: Aimless hustler becomes the neighbourhood's champion
character_outcome: Defeats Ronnie and rallies the community
critical_reception: A commercial success; the train-race sequence won Filmfare's Best Scene of the Year.
recognition: Aamir Khan's own song 'Aati Kya Khandala' earned him a Filmfare Best Male Playback Singer nomination.
research_notes: Wikipedia's ₹24.2 crore box office (Box Office India) has no nett/gross label and is not entered. The train dare and Alisha's link to a motorcycle gang come from web search summaries; Wikipedia records a breakup but not whether the couple reunite.

title: Mann
source_material: Inspired by An Affair to Remember (1957)
character_social_background: Flamboyant, debt-ridden playboy engaged to a tycoon's daughter for money
role_gist: Dev, a debt-ridden playboy painter engaged to a tycoon's daughter for money, meets Priya on a cruise; she is engaged too. They fall in love and agree to settle their affairs and meet on Valentine's Day in six months. Dev breaks his engagement and works to succeed, but Priya loses her legs in an accident on the way to meet him and hides it; he discovers the truth and marries her.
principal_motivation: Win Priya and become worthy of her
principal_conflict: Believes Priya rejected him, unaware of her accident
character_arc: Mercenary casanova becomes a faithful, self-made artist
character_outcome: Marries Priya
critical_reception: Positive reviews; the soundtrack was well received but accused of plagiarising international songs.
recognition: Soundtrack sold about 2.8 million units, the year's sixth-highest seller.
research_notes: Wikipedia's ₹35.45 crore box office (Box Office India) has no nett/gross label and is not entered. Dev's broken engagement to Anita Singhania (Deepti Bhatnagar) is recorded here rather than as a Romances row. Indra Kumar's Wikipedia article calls Mann a commercial failure, contradicting the film article's 'profitable'; no verdict entered.

title: Earth
source_material: Based on Bapsi Sidhwa's novel Cracking India (first published as Ice Candy Man)
character: Dil Navaz, the Ice Candy Man
character_social_background: Muslim man in 1947 Lahore, part of a mixed-faith circle of friends
role_gist: Dil Navaz, the Ice Candy Man, belongs to a mixed-faith circle gathered around Shanta, a nanny in Lahore, and competes for her with Hassan, the masseur she plans to marry. The sight of a train of massacred refugees during Partition turns his hurt into communal hatred. He tricks the child Lenny into revealing where Shanta is hiding, delivering her to a mob.
principal_motivation: Win Shanta
principal_conflict: Rejected love and grief poisoned by Partition violence
character_arc: Charming suitor becomes a vengeful betrayer
character_outcome: Betrays Shanta to a mob
critical_reception: Strong international reviews (86% on Rotten Tomatoes); Roger Ebert gave three of four stars, and Rediff called it probably the best performance of Aamir Khan's life.
recognition: India's submission for the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film; Filmfare debut awards for Rahul Khanna and Nandita Das.
research_notes: Indo-Canadian production. Premiered at the Toronto festival on 11 September 1998 (Wikipedia lists it as a 1998 film); released in India as 1947: Earth on 10 September 1999 (Bollywood Hungama), used as the primary release date. Box-office figures not found.

title: Mela
writers: Suneel Darshan (story); Neeraj Vora, Sanjeev Duggal, Robin Bhatt (screenplay); Neeraj Vora, Dharmesh Darshan (dialogue)
source_material: Original; the director cited Caravan (1971) as an inspiration
song_composer: Anu Malik; Rajesh Roshan; Lesle Lewis
character_social_background: Performer in a travelling troupe with his partner Shankar
role_gist: Kishan, a touring performer, first meets Roopa when she steals his clothes, then fights off goons harassing her and makes her the heroine of his dance show. Roopa feigns love to win his help against the bandit Gujjar Singh, who killed her brother and wants her as his mistress. Heartbroken when she confesses, Kishan leaves, then returns with a police ally to trap and defeat Gujjar.
principal_motivation: Love for Roopa
principal_conflict: The bandit Gujjar Singh and Roopa's strategic deception
character_arc: Carefree entertainer becomes a protector
character_outcome: Defeats Gujjar and ends with Roopa
critical_reception: Mixed reviews; Rediff called Aamir Khan the film's saving grace, while song placement and Twinkle Khanna's dubbed voice were criticised.
research_notes: Wikipedia gives 'est. ₹18 crore' budget and 'est. ₹25 crore' box office (Box Office India) without a nett/gross label; neither is entered because both are estimates and the box-office measure is unlabeled. Aishwarya Rai appears specially as Champakali, paired with Shankar (Faisal Khan). Dharmesh Darshan's Wikipedia article calls Mela a major commercial disaster with highly negative reviews; no verdict entered.

title: Lagaan
writers: Ashutosh Gowariker (story, screenplay); Kumar Dave, Sanjay Dayma (screenplay); K. P. Saxena (Hindi dialogue)
source_material: Original
character_social_background: Villager of drought-stricken Champaner in British India, 1893
role_gist: Bhuvan, a young farmer in drought-stricken Champaner in 1893, accepts Captain Russell's wager: beat the British at cricket and the tax is lifted, or pay triple. He builds a team across caste and faith, including the untouchable Kachra, is secretly coached by Russell's sister Elizabeth, survives Lakha's betrayal, and hits the winning six on the final ball before marrying Gauri.
principal_motivation: Free his village from crushing taxation
principal_conflict: The cricket wager against Captain Russell
character_arc: Defiant farmer becomes a unifying leader
character_outcome: Wins the match and marries Gauri
critical_reception: Near-universal acclaim: 95% on Rotten Tomatoes and 84 on Metacritic; Roger Ebert gave 3.5 of 4 stars.
recognition: Nominated for the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film; eight Filmfare Awards (including Best Film, Director and Actor) and eight National Film Awards; Locarno audience prize; listed in Channel 4's 50 Films to See Before You Die and Empire's 100 Best Films of World Cinema.
research_notes: Box Office India via Wikipedia. Worldwide gross ₹65.97 crore for the 2001 release; ₹67.68 crore including the 2003 China release (₹1.71 crore), which is the figure entered. Budget ₹250 million, then the highest for an Indian film.

title: Mangal Pandey: The Rising
producers: Aamir Khan; Bobby Bedi; Deepa Sahi
source_material: Life of Mangal Pandey and the start of the 1857 Indian Rebellion
character_occupation: Sepoy in the 34th Bengal Native Infantry
character_social_background: Brahmin soldier in the East India Company army
role_gist: Mangal Pandey, a loyal Brahmin sepoy who once saved Captain William Gordon's life, befriends the officer across the colonial divide. Rumours that new rifle cartridges are greased with pig and cow fat, together with the Company's wider abuses, turn him against his masters; he ends the friendship and opens fire in mutiny. Court-martialled despite Gordon's defence, he marries Heera in his cell and is hanged, inspiring revolt.
principal_motivation: Religious dignity and resistance to Company rule
principal_conflict: The greased-cartridge crisis and his friendship with Gordon
character_arc: Trusting soldier becomes a rebel martyr
character_outcome: Hanged; his execution sparks wider rebellion
critical_reception: Mostly positive (85% of 13 critics on Rotten Tomatoes); Taran Adarsh praised it, while Raja Sen dismissed it as 'cleavage and cliche'. Political parties objected to its depiction of Pandey visiting a brothel.
recognition: Screened at the Marché du Film, Cannes 2005; marked Aamir Khan's return after four years; Filmfare Best Actor nomination.
research_notes: Box Office India via Wikipedia: India ₹39.92 crore (label not stated, not entered) and worldwide ₹52.57 crore. Historian Kim A. Wagner criticised the film's lack of historical evidence. Ameesha Patel's Jwala is paired with Gordon, not Pandey.

title: Rang De Basanti
production_banner: Rakeysh Omprakash Mehra Pictures; UTV Motion Pictures
writers: Kamlesh Pandey (story); Rensil D'Silva, Rakeysh Omprakash Mehra (screenplay); Prasoon Joshi (dialogue)
alternate_identity: Plays Chandrashekhar Azad in the film-within-the-film
character_social_background: Punjabi family in Delhi; son of Mitro Kaur
role_gist: DJ is the cynical, fun-loving leader of a group of Delhi students cast by British filmmaker Sue McKinley as revolutionaries, himself playing Chandrashekhar Azad. As rehearsals draw them toward the freedom fighters' ideals, their friend Flight Lieutenant Ajay dies in a MiG-21 crash tied to corruption. The friends turn to violence against those responsible and seize All India Radio to explain themselves; DJ is shot dead.
principal_motivation: Justice for Ajay's death
principal_conflict: Official corruption behind the crash
character_arc: Apathetic youth becomes a committed, doomed rebel
character_outcome: Shot dead during the radio-station occupation
critical_reception: Overwhelmingly positive, particularly for the ensemble; the BBC gave five stars.
recognition: National Film Award for Best Popular Film; BAFTA nomination; India's Academy Award submission; Filmfare Best Film and Best Actor (Critics) for Aamir Khan; credited with inspiring youth activism, the so-called 'RDB effect'.
research_notes: Commercial figures conflict within Wikipedia: domestic ₹1.23 billion, worldwide 'more than ₹1.36 billion', and an infobox total of ₹97.90 crore; none is entered. Budget ₹250 million plus ₹100 million marketing. DJ's relationship with Sue rests on one plot sentence.

title: Fanaa
alternate_identity: Delhi tour guide by cover; secretly a commander of the militant IKF
character_social_background: Grandson of the IKF's leader
role_gist: Rehan, a charming Delhi tour guide, woos Zooni, a blind Kashmiri woman visiting with friends, and spends her last night in the city with her. He is secretly a separatist militant and fakes his death after a bombing. Seven years later he arrives wounded at the remote home where Zooni, now sighted, is raising their son. Torn between family and cause, he kills her father and is shot by Zooni as he tries to deliver a nuclear trigger.
principal_motivation: The separatist cause; later love for Zooni and their son
principal_conflict: Love for Zooni against loyalty to the militant cause
character_arc: Seductive deceiver is torn between family and terror and cannot abandon the cause
character_outcome: Shot dead by Zooni
critical_reception: Mixed to positive: praised for the lead performances and visuals, criticised as melodramatic and implausible.
recognition: Filmfare Best Actress (Kajol), Best Lyricist and Best Male Playback for 'Chand Sifarish'; Kajol's return after five years; banned in Gujarat after Aamir Khan's remarks on the Narmada dam.
research_notes: Worldwide gross ₹105.48 crore (Box Office India via Wikipedia). Wikipedia's domestic figures ('₹72.04 million gross, ₹51.87 million nett') appear to use the wrong unit and are not entered. Screen Awards nominated Aamir Khan for Best Villain.

title: Taare Zameen Par
lyricist: Prasoon Joshi; Amole Gupte; Shailendra Barve
character_occupation: Substitute art teacher at a boarding school; formerly taught children with developmental disabilities
role_gist: Nikumbh, a cheerful substitute art teacher, joins the boarding school where eight-year-old Ishaan is failing and withdrawing. Recognising dyslexia in the boy's artwork and schoolwork, he challenges the father's denial, works patiently with Ishaan on reading and helps him regain his confidence. Having struggled as a child himself, he stays on as a permanent teacher.
principal_motivation: Help Ishaan overcome dyslexia
principal_conflict: The father's and school's dismissal of the diagnosis
character_arc: Temporary substitute becomes a transformative mentor
character_outcome: Ishaan flourishes; Nikumbh joins the permanent staff
critical_reception: Widespread critical acclaim (93% on Rotten Tomatoes).
recognition: Aamir Khan's directorial debut; Filmfare Best Film and Best Director; National Film Award for Best Film on Family Welfare; India's Academy Award submission; credited with raising dyslexia awareness and prompting extra exam time for disabled students.
research_notes: Wikipedia treats Darsheel Safary's Ishaan as the protagonist; Aamir Khan was nominated for Filmfare Best Supporting Actor. Worldwide grosses conflict: ₹88.97 crore (Box Office India), ₹98.48 crore (Bollywood Hungama), ₹107 crore (Box Office Mojo), ₹131 crore (Telegraph) and ₹135 crore (Indian Express); none entered. Amole Gupte was originally to direct.

title: Ghajini
producers: Allu Aravind; Tagore B. Madhu; Madhu Mantena
writers: A. R. Murugadoss (story, screenplay); Aamir Khan (screenplay); Piyush Mishra (dialogue)
source_material: Remake of the Tamil film Ghajini (2005); memory device inspired by Memento (2000)
alternate_identity: Poses as a struggling model called Sachin Chauhan
character_occupation: Chairman of the telecom company Air Voice
character_social_background: Wealthy second-generation businessman
role_gist: Sanjay, a telecom tycoon, courts the generous Kalpana while posing as a struggling model called Sachin, and proposes to her. When she rescues girls from a trafficking ring, its boss Ghajini ambushes her and kills her in front of Sanjay, leaving him with anterograde amnesia. Using photographs, notes and tattoos, Sanjay hunts Ghajini down and kills him with the same iron rod.
principal_motivation: Avenge Kalpana's murder
principal_conflict: Hunting her killer while losing his memory every fifteen minutes
character_arc: Romantic tycoon becomes a vengeful amnesiac, then finds peace
character_outcome: Kills Ghajini; later volunteers at an orphanage named after Kalpana
critical_reception: Mixed to positive (54% on Rotten Tomatoes): praised as entertaining and for Aamir Khan's performance, criticised for its length and violence.
recognition: First Hindi film to cross ₹100 crore nett in India, creating the '100 crore club'; year's best-selling soundtrack; Filmfare Best Female Debut for Asin.
research_notes: Wikipedia gives a ₹52 crore budget in the infobox and ₹65 crore in the text; entered as a range. Domestic nett is an estimate from Box Office India. Overseas and worldwide grosses not stated. Sunita (Jiah Khan) is a confidante, not a romantic interest.

title: Luck by Chance
role_gist: Aamir Khan is one of the film-industry figures who appear as themselves in Zoya Akhtar's debut, a drama about newcomers trying to break into Bollywood that shows the industry's lesser-seen side. The sources consulted list him among the guest appearances but do not describe his scene.
critical_reception: Widespread critical acclaim (83% on Rotten Tomatoes).
recognition: Filmfare Best Debut Director for Zoya Akhtar (tied).
research_notes: Budget ₹150 million; box office 'est. ₹290 million' has no nett/gross label and is not entered.

title: 3 Idiots
source_material: Adapted from Chetan Bhagat's novel Five Point Someone (story credit disputed)
background_score_composer: Shantanu Moitra; Atul Raninga; Sanjay Wandrekar
alternate_identity: Real identity Phunsukh Wangdu; studied under his employer's son's name
character_occupation: Engineering student; later inventor and educator in Ladakh
character_social_background: Gardener's son educated in place of a wealthy family's son
role_gist: Rancho, a brilliant engineering student who scorns rote learning, befriends Farhan and Raju and clashes with the director Viru 'Virus' Sahastrabuddhe, whose daughter Pia he loves. After a classmate's suicide and a baby delivery Rancho improvises during a blackout, he graduates and vanishes. Years later his friends find him in Ladakh as the celebrated inventor Phunsukh Wangdu, and Pia reunites with him.
principal_motivation: Learning for passion rather than marks
principal_conflict: The rote-learning system embodied by Virus
character_arc: Idealistic student becomes an inventor-educator who proves his philosophy
character_outcome: Revealed as Phunsukh Wangdu and reunited with Pia
critical_reception: Widespread acclaim in India and abroad (100% of 15 critics on Rotten Tomatoes).
recognition: Six Filmfare Awards including Best Film and Director; National Film Award for Best Popular Film; highest-grossing Indian film until 2013; Guinness World Records listing; remade in Tamil (Nanban) and Mexico (3 Idiotas); influential on education debates in India, China and South Korea.
research_notes: Budget ₹55 crore per Wikipedia; IANS estimated ₹35–45 crore. Overseas gross given as US$30.5 million (₹186 crore).

title: Dhobi Ghat
character_social_background: Divorced artist whose ex-wife and child live in Australia
role_gist: Arun, a reclusive divorced painter, has a one-night stand with the banker and photographer Shai and coldly ends it the next morning. In his new flat he finds three video diaries left by the previous tenant, Yasmin, and becomes absorbed in her loneliness and her husband's infidelity. When the last tape suggests she meant to take her own life, he flees the flat and turns her story into a painting.
principal_motivation: Solitude and his art; later understanding Yasmin
principal_conflict: Emotional detachment and fixation on a dead stranger's diaries
character_arc: Detached artist is shaken into grief and creation
character_outcome: Moves out and completes a painting of Yasmin
critical_reception: Critically well received (70% on Rotten Tomatoes), though some reviewers called it pretentious.
recognition: Kiran Rao's directorial debut; premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival (September 2010); longlisted for the BAFTA for Best Film Not in the English Language.
research_notes: Theatrical release 21 January 2011 after the 2010 Toronto premiere. Wikipedia's ₹40 crore budget conflicts with Aamir Khan's statement that the film made double its cost on a ₹25.6 crore global gross; budget not entered.

title: Delhi Belly
producers: Aamir Khan; Kiran Rao; Ronnie Screwvala; Jim Furgele
production_banner: Aamir Khan Productions; UTV Motion Pictures
lyricist: Amitabh Bhattacharya; Munna Dhiman; Ram Sampath; Akshat Verma; Chetan Shashital
role_gist: Aamir Khan appears as 'Disco Fighter' in the song 'I Hate You (Like I Love You)', which plays over the closing credits of this black comedy starring Imran Khan, Vir Das and Kunaal Roy Kapur, which he co-produced. The cameo is outside the story.
critical_reception: Widespread acclaim as an original ensemble comedy; the song 'Bhaag D.K. Bose' drew controversy.
recognition: Filmfare Best Screenplay (Akshat Verma).
research_notes: Wikipedia's ₹87.60 crore box office has no nett/gross label and is not entered.

title: Talaash: The Answer Lies Within
producers: Ritesh Sidhwani; Aamir Khan; Farhan Akhtar
writers: Reema Kagti, Zoya Akhtar (story, screenplay); Farhan Akhtar, Anurag Kashyap (dialogue)
character_social_background: Grieving father whose eight-year-old son Karan drowned
role_gist: Surjan, a Mumbai inspector sleepless with guilt over his young son's drowning, investigates the death of a film star whose car plunged into the sea. His marriage to Roshni is frozen by grief, and he scorns her visits to a psychic. Helped by the escort Rosie, he uncovers a buried hit-and-run and realises Rosie is the victim's ghost; after cremating her remains, he accepts his son's forgiveness and reconciles with Roshni.
principal_motivation: Solve the case and escape his grief
principal_conflict: Guilt over his son's death against a case that leads into the supernatural
character_arc: Rational, grief-frozen detective accepts loss and the inexplicable
character_outcome: Solves the case and reconciles with Roshni
critical_reception: Positive (81% on Rotten Tomatoes); some critics found the twist derivative of The Sixth Sense.
recognition: Filmfare nominations for Rani Mukerji and Nawazuddin Siddiqui.
research_notes: Box Office India via Wikipedia: domestic nett about ₹93 crore; overseas gross US$8.5 million; worldwide estimated at ₹174.21–180.83 crore, combining domestic nett with overseas gross, so the worldwide figure mixes measures and is entered as text.

title: Bombay Talkies
director: Karan Johar; Dibakar Banerjee; Zoya Akhtar; Anurag Kashyap
production_banner: Flying Unicorn Entertainment; Dharma Productions; Dibakar Banerjee Productions; Excel Entertainment; AKFPL; Sikhya Entertainment
role_gist: Aamir Khan appears as himself among many stars in the song 'Apna Bombay Talkies', which celebrates the centenary of Indian cinema in this four-part anthology by Karan Johar, Dibakar Banerjee, Zoya Akhtar and Anurag Kashyap. The appearance sits outside the anthology's stories.
critical_reception: Positive reviews; screened at the 2013 Cannes Film Festival.
recognition: Made for the 100th year of Indian cinema; Karan Johar's segment received a Queer Palm nomination.
research_notes: Wikipedia's estimated earnings of ₹10 crore have no nett/gross label and are not entered.

title: Dhoom 3
writers: Vijay Krishna Acharya (screenplay); Aditya Chopra, Vijay Krishna Acharya (story)
character_social_background: Sons of Iqbal Khan, whose Chicago circus was foreclosed by a bank
role_gist: As a boy, Sahir watches his father kill himself when the Western Bank of Chicago forecloses on their circus. Grown up, he robs the bank in daring heists with his secret twin Samar, whose existence is hidden. Indian detectives Jai and Ali close in by exploiting Samar's romance with the acrobat Aaliya. Cornered on a dam, Samar will not let go of Sahir's hand, and the brothers fall to their deaths together.
principal_motivation: Revenge on the bank that ruined their father
principal_conflict: Exposure of the twin secret
character_arc: Revenge-driven showmen are undone by love and loyalty
character_outcome: Both die falling from the dam
critical_reception: Mixed reviews in India, more favourable abroad (67% on Rotten Tomatoes); critics compared it with The Prestige.
recognition: First Indian film to gross ₹500 crore worldwide; highest-grossing Indian film on release; Filmfare Best Visual Effects.
research_notes: Worldwide gross reported as ₹556.74–558.42 crore; the lower figure is entered. Domestic nett combines ₹261 crore (Hindi) and ₹11.5 crore (Tamil and Telugu). Domestic and overseas grosses (₹372 crore + ₹217.2 crore) do not sum to the worldwide total; figures come from different sources. Samar is Aaliya's partner.

title: PK
production_banner: Vinod Chopra Films; Rajkumar Hirani Films
lyricist: Swanand Kirkire; Amitabh Varma; Manoj Muntashir
character_social_background: Humanoid alien with no knowledge of human customs
role_gist: PK, a humanoid alien on a research mission, is stranded in Rajasthan when a thief steals the remote that summons his spaceship. Told that only God can help, he tries the rituals of every religion and concludes that godmen are dialling a 'wrong number'. With the journalist Jaggu he exposes the godman Tapasvi, who holds his remote, reunites her with her lost love Sarfaraz, suppresses his own love for her and leaves Earth.
principal_motivation: Recover his remote and return home
principal_conflict: Religious exploitation, embodied by the godman Tapasvi
character_arc: Naive outsider becomes a social critic who gives up his own love
character_outcome: Returns home; later leads a new expedition to Earth
critical_reception: Widely praised (NDTV five stars; Bollywood Hungama 4.5/5); Hindu nationalist groups protested, and complaints were filed over religious sentiment.
recognition: Highest-grossing Indian film on release and the first to gross over ₹700 crore and US$100 million worldwide; Filmfare Best Screenplay and Dialogue.
research_notes: Box Office India via Wikipedia. Distributor share ₹165 crore and entertainment tax ₹107.94 crore reported separately. Domestic plus overseas gross (₹753.26 crore) does not equal the stated worldwide figure; sources differ.

title: Dil Dhadakne Do
writers: Reema Kagti, Zoya Akhtar (screenplay); Farhan Akhtar (dialogue)
alternate_identity: Voices the family dog, who narrates the film
role_gist: Aamir Khan voices Pluto, the Mehra family's dog, who narrates this ensemble comedy-drama about a dysfunctional family and offers wry commentary on human behaviour. He does not appear on screen. Reviewers found that the narration added philosophical depth to Zoya Akhtar's film, whose cast includes Anil Kapoor, Shefali Shah, Priyanka Chopra and Ranveer Singh.
critical_reception: Positive reviews for the cast and direction, with criticism of the length and climax.
recognition: Filmfare Best Supporting Actor (Anil Kapoor).
research_notes: Budget ₹550 million; box office ₹1.44 billion has no nett/gross label and is not entered. Pluto is both a character and the film's narrator.

title: Secret Superstar
producers: Aamir Khan; Kiran Rao; Nitin Keni; Akash Chawla
character_social_background: Talented but pretentious industry figure going through a divorce
role_gist: Shakti Kumar, a talented but pretentious music director in the middle of a divorce, discovers the teenage singer Insia through her YouTube channel and brings her to Mumbai to record. His slapstick vanity gradually gives way to genuine mentorship, and he publicly acknowledges her achievement at an awards ceremony.
principal_motivation: Revive his flagging career
principal_conflict: His ego and scandal-prone reputation
character_arc: Self-absorbed has-been becomes a supportive mentor
character_outcome: Champions Insia's success
critical_reception: Strongly positive (92% on Rotten Tomatoes); Aamir Khan's comic performance was singled out.
recognition: Filmfare Best Actress (Critics) for Zaira Wasim and Best Supporting Actress for Meher Vij; one of the most profitable Indian films; the second-highest-grossing non-English foreign film in China at the time.
research_notes: Worldwide estimates range from ₹858.43 crore to ₹966 crore; ₹905.7 crore (US$154 million) is entered as the most specific figure. China gross about ₹751 crore; other overseas ₹65 crore. Aamir Khan received a Filmfare Best Supporting Actor nomination.

title: Thugs of Hindostan
source_material: Original story set against historical events; not based on Confessions of a Thug
character_occupation: Con man and East India Company informer
character_social_background: Small-time thug from Awadh
role_gist: Firangi, a slippery con man from Awadh, infiltrates Khudabaksh's rebel thugs as an informer for the East India Company's John Clive. He double-crosses both sides for money, but loyalty to the rebels grows on him: he saves Khudabaksh from a fall and takes a bullet for the warrior Zafira. After helping defeat Clive, he steals a ship and sails off with the dancer Suraiyya and his friend Shanichar.
principal_motivation: Money
principal_conflict: Divided loyalty between the Company and the rebels
character_arc: Mercenary trickster becomes a reluctant ally of the rebellion
character_outcome: Escapes by ship with Suraiyya and Shanichar
verdict: Commercial failure after a record opening
critical_reception: Generally negative in India, faulting direction, screenplay and length; more favourable overseas.
recognition: Record opening day for a Hindi film (₹52.25 crore nett).
research_notes: Budget estimates: ₹200 crore (NDTV, Zee Business), ₹220 crore (Bollywood Hungama), ₹300 crore (Hindustan Times, News18). Worldwide estimates ₹322.07 crore and ₹335 crore. Second-billed after Amitabh Bachchan. Firangi's flirtation with Suraiyya (Katrina Kaif) and his bond with Zafira (Fatima Sana Shaikh) are too thinly documented for Romances rows.

title: Koi Jaane Na
producers: Bhushan Kumar; Krishan Kumar; Amin Hajee
song_composer: Tanishk Bagchi; Amaal Mallik; Rochak Kohli; Vikram Negi
role_gist: Aamir Khan makes a special appearance in the song 'Har Funn Maula' with Elli AvrRam in this psychological thriller starring Kunal Kapoor and Amyra Dastur. Wikipedia's filmography credits him as himself; the song has no bearing on the plot, which stars Kunal Kapoor and Amyra Dastur.
research_notes: No box-office, reception or award data found.

title: Laal Singh Chaddha
producers: Aamir Khan; Kiran Rao; Jyoti Deshpande; Ajit Andhare
production_banner: Aamir Khan Productions; Viacom18 Studios; Paramount Pictures
source_material: Adaptation of Forrest Gump (1994), based on Winston Groom's novel
alternate_identity: Also plays his ancestors Veer, Jagan and Manav Singh Chaddha
character_social_background: Sikh family from a village near Pathankot; raised by a devoted mother
role_gist: Laal, a kind-hearted Sikh boy with a low IQ and leg braces, discovers he can run and believes, as his mother taught him, that he can achieve anything. His life crosses decades of Indian history: army service in the Kargil War, a Vir Chakra, friendship with Bala and a successful business. Throughout, he loves his childhood friend Rupa, who chases fame through troubled relationships, until she returns ill and they marry before her death.
principal_motivation: Love for Rupa and his mother's faith in him
principal_conflict: Rupa repeatedly leaves him for a different life
character_arc: Bullied child becomes soldier, entrepreneur, husband and father
character_outcome: Marries Rupa and raises their son Aman
critical_reception: Mixed (69% on Rotten Tomatoes, 46 on Metacritic): praised for its adaptation and music, criticised for pacing, length and Aamir Khan's performance.
recognition: Ten Filmfare nominations including Best Actress for Kareena Kapoor; strong global Netflix viewing; the target of a boycott campaign before release.
research_notes: Box Office India via Wikipedia; the domestic figure is recorded as gross because domestic plus overseas equals the stated worldwide gross. The Indian Express estimated losses of ₹100 crore.

title: Salaam Venky
production_banner: Connekkt Media; Blive Productions; RTake Studios
writers: Shrikant Murthy (story); Sammeer Arora (screenplay); Kausar Munir (dialogue)
source_material: Based on the true story of Kolavennu Venkatesh and Shrikant Murthy's novel The Last Hurrah
role_gist: Aamir Khan makes a cameo as an illusion seen by Sujata, the mother played by Kajol, in this drama based on the true story of Kolavennu Venkatesh and his mother. The sources consulted do not describe the length or content of the scene.
critical_reception: Mixed: 25% of eight critics on Rotten Tomatoes, though The Times of India gave four stars.
research_notes: Bollywood Hungama's ₹1.99 crore box office has no nett/gross label and is not entered.

title: Sitaare Zameen Par
source_material: Official remake of the Spanish film Campeones (Champions, 2018)
character_social_background: Lives with his mother Preeto; married to Sunita
role_gist: Gulshan, an arrogant, disillusioned assistant basketball coach, is sentenced to community service for drunk driving: he must train a team of intellectually disabled players. Impatient and condescending at first, he slowly learns each player's struggles and strengths, helps Guddu overcome his fear of bathing, confronts his own phobia and comes to see the team as his teachers, while accepting the fatherhood he had resisted.
principal_motivation: Complete a court-ordered sentence; later his team's success
principal_conflict: His own prejudice and impatience toward his players
character_arc: Arrogant, self-centred coach becomes humble and emotionally open
character_outcome: Transformed by the team and ready to become a father
critical_reception: Positive reviews (63% on Rotten Tomatoes) for Aamir Khan's committed performance and its warmth, with criticism that it is preachy and less affecting than Taare Zameen Par.
recognition: Released with closed captions, audio description and Indian Sign Language together; after its theatrical run it was released on YouTube for ₹100 in India instead of going straight to a streaming service.
research_notes: Wikipedia's 'est. ₹266.49 crore' box office is not labelled worldwide, gross or nett in the source summary and is not entered. Reported as the seventh-highest-grossing Hindi film of 2025. Awards not listed on the page as of the research date.

title: Coolie
character_occupation: Leader of a global crime syndicate
role_gist: In his first Tamil film, Aamir Khan makes a cameo as Dahaa, revealed as the leader of a global syndicate and the son of the villain Kakkar, in Lokesh Kanagaraj's Rajinikanth action thriller. He has said he accepted the part without reading the script because he admires Rajinikanth. The sources do not describe the cameo's length or reception.
critical_reception: Mixed reviews (63% on Rotten Tomatoes); Rajinikanth and the action were praised, the narrative less so.
research_notes: Budget and worldwide-gross estimates vary widely and are entered as ranges. Released with Telugu, Hindi and Kannada dubs. Wikipedia's filmography describes the role as a special appearance.

title: Happy Patel: Khatarnak Jasoos
producers: Aamir Khan; Aparna Purohit; Vir Das; Kavi Shastri
role_gist: Aamir Khan makes a cameo as Jimmy Mario in this spy comedy directed by and starring Vir Das, which he also produced. The sources consulted give the character's name but not the length or content of his scenes. Vir Das plays the title role opposite Mithila Palkar, with Mona Singh and Sharib Hashmi in support.
critical_reception: Mixed (45% of 11 critics on Rotten Tomatoes): called messy and unfocused by some, chaotic fun by others.
research_notes: Wikipedia's ₹6.84 crore box office has no nett/gross label and is not entered. Runtime, writers and composers not captured.

title: Qayamat Se Qayamat Tak
writers: Nasir Hussain (story, screenplay); Nuzhat Khan, Aamir Khan (assistant writers)
source_material: Original; modern retelling of Layla–Majnun, Heer–Ranjha and Romeo and Juliet
alternate_identity: Poses as Roop Singh, Rashmi's intended suitor, at her birthday party
character_occupation: Graduate who joins the family clothing business
character_social_background: Rajput family from Dhanakpur, raised in Delhi by his uncle after his father's imprisonment for murder
role_gist: Raj, the college-educated son of a Rajput family broken by a murder, falls for Rashmi without knowing she belongs to the clan his father wronged. He gatecrashes her birthday under a false name, courts her on holiday and, when both families forbid the match, elopes with her to a ruined fort. Hired killers shoot Rashmi; Raj stabs himself and dies beside her.
principal_motivation: Love for Rashmi and a life free of the family feud
principal_conflict: Loves the daughter of his family's sworn enemy
character_arc: Dutiful, wholesome son becomes a lover who defies both families and chooses death over separation
character_outcome: Dies by suicide beside Rashmi after she is shot
critical_reception: Positive reviews; credited with reinventing the romantic musical and bringing family audiences back to cinemas.
recognition: Cult classic with a 50-week run; subject of a 2016 book crediting it with reviving Hindi cinema; remade in Telugu, Bangladeshi Bengali, Sinhala and Nepali.
research_notes: Budget ₹25 million and domestic nett ₹50 million (The Times of India, via Wikipedia). Wikipedia also lists ₹50 million as worldwide gross without a separate source; not recorded because it duplicates the nett figure. Annual rank 3 (behind Tezaab and Shahenshah) per Box Office India via Wikipedia.

title: Dil Hai Ke Manta Nahin
source_material: Adaptation of It Happened One Night (1934) and Chori Chori (1956)
lyricist: Sameer; Faaiz Anwar; Rani Malik; Aziz Khan
character_occupation: Journalist who has just lost his job
character_social_background: Working-class and financially insecure
role_gist: Raghu, a newly unemployed journalist, recognises a runaway heiress on a bus and forces a bargain: he will help her reach her film-star fiancé in exchange for an exclusive story. The road trip turns bickering into love. When he leaves to raise money so he can propose, she believes he has used her and returns to marry the star, until her father reveals Raghu's integrity.
principal_motivation: An exclusive story to rescue his career, then love for Pooja
principal_conflict: Has no money or standing to marry the heiress he has fallen for
character_arc: Opportunistic blackmailer becomes a devoted, scrupulous lover
character_outcome: Pooja leaves her wedding to marry him with her father's blessing
critical_reception: A commercial success whose soundtrack was praised; boosted Pooja Bhatt's career and consolidated Aamir Khan's stardom.
recognition: Remade in Telugu as Kurradi Kurrodu (1994) and Tamil as Kadhal Rojavae (2000).
research_notes: Wikipedia gives box office of ₹42 million (₹4.2 crore) citing Box Office India, without saying whether it is nett or gross; Box Office India's own film page shows no figures. Not entered in any commercial column. Runtime from Box Office India. Filmfare: Best Actor nomination for Aamir Khan.

title: Sarfarosh
writers: John Matthew Matthan (story, screenplay); Hriday Lani, Pathik Vats (dialogue)
source_material: Original; drew on 1990s state-sponsored terrorism in India
lyricist: Israr Ansari; Nida Fazli; Sameer; Indeevar
character_occupation: Assistant Commissioner of Police leading a special investigation
character_social_background: Middle-class family scarred by terrorism: brother killed, father left mute
role_gist: Ajay joins the police after terrorists kill his brother and leave his father unable to speak. As an ACP he tracks an arms-smuggling network while resented by the senior Inspector Saleem, and slowly discovers that his admired friend Gulfam Hassan is a Pakistani intelligence agent. Recovering from wounds, he tricks Gulfam into self-incrimination and destroys the network; his reunion with college crush Seema is a warm secondary thread.
principal_motivation: Fight the terrorism that destroyed his family
principal_conflict: Exposing a trusted friend as the mastermind of the arms network
character_arc: Idealistic, inexperienced officer learns to pair integrity with cunning
character_outcome: Dismantles the network and is honoured in Mumbai
critical_reception: Critical acclaim; Filmfare gave four stars for its characterisation and performances, and Naseeruddin Shah was especially praised.
recognition: National Film Award for Best Popular Film Providing Wholesome Entertainment; screened at IFFI; remade in Kannada and Telugu. Zee Cine Best Actor for Aamir Khan.
research_notes: Wikipedia gives box office of ₹33.46 crore citing Box Office India without a nett/gross label; not entered in a commercial column. Budget ₹8 crore.

title: Dil Chahta Hai
source_material: Original; drawn from Farhan Akhtar's travel diaries with inputs from Kassim Jagmagia
character_occupation: Heir working in his family's Sydney-based business
character_social_background: Wealthy upper-class Mumbai family
role_gist: Akash is the flippant, wisecracking member of a trio of affluent Mumbai friends who treats love as a joke. Posted to his family's business in Sydney, he spends time with Shalini, who is engaged to his college batchmate Rohit, and realises he loves her only after she returns to India for her wedding. He comes home to declare himself, and she leaves the wedding to be with him.
principal_motivation: A carefree life with his friends, then winning Shalini
principal_conflict: Falls for a woman committed to marry someone else
character_arc: Detached cynic who mocks romance becomes emotionally open and vulnerable
character_outcome: United with Shalini and reconciled with his friends
critical_reception: Widespread critical acclaim for its fresh narrative, direction, performances and realistic portrayal of urban youth; Saif Ali Khan and Akshaye Khanna particularly praised.
recognition: Cult status; credited with launching a new wave of urban Hindi cinema. National Film Award for Best Feature Film in Hindi; seven Filmfare Awards including Best Film (Critics).
research_notes: Box Office India via Wikipedia: domestic ₹332.8 million, overseas ₹64.4 million, worldwide gross ₹397.2 million. The domestic figure is recorded as gross because domestic plus overseas equals the stated worldwide gross. Annual rank refers to domestic earnings.

title: Dangal
producers: Aamir Khan; Kiran Rao; Siddharth Roy Kapur
production_banner: Aamir Khan Productions; The Walt Disney Company India
writers: Nitesh Tiwari; Piyush Gupta; Shreyas Jain; Nikhil Mehrotra
source_material: True story of Mahavir Singh Phogat and his daughters Geeta and Babita
character_occupation: Former national wrestling champion turned coach of his daughters
character_social_background: Rural Haryana (Balali); gave up wrestling for a steady job under family pressure
role_gist: Mahavir, a former national wrestling champion pushed by his father to take a steady job, wants a son to win the international gold he never could. After four daughters, he recognises Geeta and Babita's strength and trains them with harsh discipline despite village ridicule. When Geeta falters under the national coach's methods, he secretly guides her again and she wins Commonwealth Games gold.
principal_motivation: Win a gold medal for India through his children
principal_conflict: Community ridicule, then a clash with the national academy coach over Geeta's training
character_arc: Resigned, disappointed father becomes an obsessive and ultimately vindicated coach
character_outcome: Geeta wins gold at the 2010 Commonwealth Games
female_leads: Sakshi Tanwar; Fatima Sana Shaikh; Sanya Malhotra
critical_reception: Universal acclaim for its honesty and Aamir Khan's performance; critics debated whether its feminism is undercut by centring the father as the true hero.
recognition: Filmfare Best Film, Director and Actor; AACTA Best Asian Film; major success in China, where it influenced audience taste and India–China cultural relations; screened in the Indian Parliament.
research_notes: The marriage to Daya (Sakshi Tanwar) has minimal narrative weight, so no Romances row. Worldwide totals disagree: Bollywood Hungama ₹1,968 crore; Box Office India ₹2,024 crore (used); Box Office Mojo ₹2,050 crore; Hindustan Times over ₹2,200 crore. Domestic ₹538.03 crore is the final all-language gross; China alone about ₹1,231 crore. The component figures come from different sources and do not sum exactly to the Box Office India total.
